header.headline: Security & responsible disclosure
header.subhead: How we secure this site, how to report a vulnerability, and the boundaries around clinical content.

sections.title: Securing this site
bullets: HTTPS enforced across all pages; modern TLS configuration.
Minimal data collection — the contact form collects only what routing requires.
Access to content and infrastructure is limited to maintainers with individual accounts and multi-factor authentication.
Dependency and content review on every pull request; releases are tagged and auditable.

sections.title: Vulnerability disclosure
sections.body: Report vulnerabilities in the landing repository or site through the GitHub Security Advisory channel (private reporting) or the security tab of the repository. Do not open a public issue for exploitable findings.
steps: Describe the issue, affected path, and reproduction steps.
Do not include real patient data in any report — use synthetic examples.
Allow reasonable time for a fix before public discussion.
We acknowledge reports promptly and keep the reporter informed.
Credit is offered unless you prefer to remain anonymous.

sections.title: Clinical content boundaries
bullets: This website is not a clinical channel. Do not send patient data through forms, issues, or discussions.
Product descriptions are architecture/roadmap statements, not clinical validation.
"Designed for" anonymization is not a certification; no regulatory clearance is claimed on this site.
Requests that ask us to facilitate unauthorised access to health data are declined.

sections.title: Product security (under agreement)
sections.body: Security architecture, data-boundary controls, deployment hardening, and support channels for the KONSENXIA product are covered in the commercial agreement and its documentation — not on this public site. Audit and certification evidence, when it exists, will be shared under NDA through the contact channel with auditor, scope, and date attached.

sections.title: Compliance note
sections.body: Website privacy posture is described in /privacy with KVKK and GDPR rights. Product-level compliance posture is recorded as architecture in docs/legal/* — design goals, not certificates.
